newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to buy 700,000 tonnes coal from Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to buy 700,000 tonnes coal from Vietnam.

text.p: Bulgaria, poor in energy resources and hamstrung by a lack of funds, will import 700,000 tonnes of high quality coal from Vietnam for the coming winter, National Electricity Company (NEC) chairman said on Wednesday.
Kozma Kuzmanov said the 1,260-megawatt Varna coal and gas-fired plant would receive the Vietnamese coal at a rate of 150,000 tonnes a month.

"Apart from the Vietnamese coal, together with Ukraine's coal supplies we will ensure the operation of all the four units of the Varna plant during the winter," Kuzmanov told a meeting of the parliamentary energy committee.
He did not say how much would be imported from Ukraine.
Kuzmanov said the NEC had signed an agreement for $4 million from ING Bank, part of Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV. The sum will go towards coal supplies payments, he said.
The NEC is among 70 indebted state companies isolated from credits while they are restructured under a government austerity programme agreed with the Intenational Monetary Fund.

The Varna plant, which did not run last winter due to a lack of funds for coal, is due to replace electricity production from the oldest 440-megawatt nuclear reactor at Kozloduy, closed for safety tests amid international concern.
In July the European Union said it would grant 10 million Ecus to Bulgaria's energy sector as compensation for closing the controversial reactor and buying coal for the Varna plant.
